Internal sub-steps: openTurn (302-313), historyTurns (325-334), tools+llmTools (337-361), adapter (375-394), relationalHistory compaction (396-413), messages assembly (415-444), initialTraces (446-463), runConversationLoop call (465-646).
findings.fix_hint: Extract: (a) buildHistoryAndMemoryPrefixes(args) -> { messages, initialTraces, historyTurns }; (b) buildRunToolsAndLlm(args) -> { tools, llmTools, toolExecutor }. Pass plain data into a slim runButlerLoopBody that only orchestrates.

findings.title: evaluateChannelApproval takes _ctx: ChannelContext but never uses it (SO-014)
findings.description: D63 audit SO-014 called this out as a god-fn split leftover. The helper accepts a ChannelContext with channel/actor/correlationId but the parameter is prefixed with `_` and discarded. The cross-channel tests only check the result; they don't assert that channel wiring actually happens. The ChannelContext is dead weight and the function name suggests cross-channel support that isn't real.
findings.evidence: inline-approval-wiring.ts:28 _ctx: ChannelContext — never referenced. tests at cross-channel.test.ts:22,35,45 pass a ctx but assert only on decision/renderPrompt output. channel-inbound.ts:36 explicitly notes 'does not call evaluateChannelApproval directly'.
findings.fix_hint: Either thread ChannelContext into the decision (e.g., add channel to the rendered prompt or audit subject) OR remove the parameter and rename to evaluateFatigueDecision. Update the cross-channel test to remove the ctx arg.

findings.title: replayFatigueSequence marks events as 'replayed' without actually invoking undo (D65+ drift)
findings.description: The function name implies real replay, but the implementation only collects event_ids into the `replayed` array. Per the inline comment (lines 112-115): 'actual undo invocation is wired in D65+ when audit_events has listRecentAuditEvents (per Task 6 GAP doc). For now we mark as replayed and log the intent.' The test R3 (replay-api.test.ts:57) only checks `expect(result.replayed).toContain('e-write')` — which passes vacuously. The owner-facing route POST /v1/owner/audit/fatigue/replay returns success even though no undo actually ran. This is a pre-scoped drift; the contract ships but the body is a stub.
findings.evidence: replay.ts:88-120 — for each reversible eventId, `replayed.push(eventId)` with no toolExecutor call, no D49 undoChain dispatch, no D46 undoLastWrite. Comment at 112-115 admits the gap.
findings.fix_hint: Either: (a) wire actual undo dispatch (D49 undoChain / D46 undoLastWrite) by eventId; (b) rename to markAsReplayable / dryRunReplay and emit a 501-like degraded response; (c) document explicitly in the route response that `replayed: []` is a no-op until the wiring ships.

findings.title: currentOwnerActor() returns literal sentinel 'owner' (SEC-013, pre-scoped for D70+)
findings.description: Hardcoded return 'owner' defeats the cross-actor security check in replayFatigueSequence (line 105). When proper owner auth with bearer is added, ownerId will come from the session. Until then, the cross-actor check is a sentinel-vs-sentinel match. audit-reader.ts:44 explicitly marks it 'TODO(D65+)' — but D70+ is the current batch.
findings.evidence: audit-fatigue.ts:39-41: function currentOwnerActor(): string { return 'owner' }. Comment on line 33-37: 'When proper owner auth with bearer is added, ownerId will come from the authenticated session...'. audit-reader.ts:44: 'CQ-035 audit-fatigue.ts TODO(D65+) for session lookup'.
findings.fix_hint: D70 pre-scoped #2 is 'Owner-route acceptance coverage' which is the natural home for this fix. The cross-actor check needs a real owner identity — D69 T4 added x-inbound-secret for wechat/telegram; an equivalent owner session token would close this gap.

findings.title: loadQualityGateConfig casts parsed JSON to QualityGateConfig without field validation
findings.description: After only `typeof parsed === 'object' && !Array.isArray(parsed)` check, the function does `return parsed as QualityGateConfig`. A malformed config file (e.g., a JSON number, or an object missing required fields) gets passed downstream. The downstream `gateProject()` accesses `?.projects?.[id]` and `truncate(text, max)`, so a non-string `description` field would crash at runtime — the cast hides the type unsoundness.
findings.evidence: wechat-quality-gate.ts:35-43: parsed: unknown = JSON.parse(...); if (!parsed || typeof parsed !== 'object' || Array.isArray(parsed)) return null; return parsed as QualityGateConfig. Same pattern in wechat-project-surface.ts:47 (return parsed as WechatProjectPathsConfig).
findings.fix_hint: Add a per-field validator (Zod schema or hand-rolled) that confirms `projects` is an object, each entry has `description: string`, etc. Return null on shape mismatch. Same fix for the 5+ other 'parsed as X' sites (project-state, wechat-project-surface, audit-log, dev-quality-gate, channel-outbound).

findings.title: loadWechatProjectPathsConfig: same parsed-as cast without per-field validation
findings.description: Pattern duplicates D70-CQ-012. The function only checks `typeof === 'object' && !Array.isArray(parsed)` and `typeof root['version'] === 'number'` — then casts the rest of the object to WechatProjectPathsConfig. Subsequent `?.projects?.[id]` accesses will throw at runtime if `projects` is missing/wrong-type.
findings.evidence: wechat-project-surface.ts:38-51. Same anti-pattern at project-state.ts:47, audit-log.ts:103, dev-quality-gate.ts:54.
findings.fix_hint: Either use Zod (consistent with elsewhere) or write a minimal hand-rolled validator that checks each required field shape. Apply uniformly across the 5 'parsed as X' sites.

findings.title: appendFileSync audit-log swallows errors with bare `catch {}` — owner-visible failures hidden
findings.description: Append failure (disk full, EACCES, etc.) is silently swallowed. The comment 'we never want a broken filesystem to crash the route' is the right intent, but no log is emitted. If the JSONL audit log stops writing for days, no one notices. The D58/D59/D60 audit explicitly closed sibling 'silent fail' findings on audit-service.ts:42 and similar — this site was missed.
findings.evidence: audit-log.ts:72-79: try { appendFileSync(auditLogPath(), JSON.stringify(entry) + '\n') } catch { /* swallow */ }. By contrast audit-service.ts:42 logs to console.error. wechat-session-state.ts:84 logs via console.error.
findings.fix_hint: Add `console.error('[audit-log] appendAudit failed:', err)` in the catch block. Mirrors the D58 T1 fix at audit-service.ts:42.

findings.title: readRecentSubagentAudit silently returns [] on JSON.parse failure
findings.description: The outer `catch {}` (line 110) returns []; the inner per-line `catch {}` (line 105) skips malformed lines. Both are silent. The function is still used by wechat-subagent-commands.ts:60 (legacy /subagent list), so a corrupted JSONL log would yield an empty list with no operator signal.
findings.evidence: audit-log.ts:88-112: safeLimit caps, existsSync guard, per-line JSON.parse try/catch silently skips, outer try/catch returns []. No log call.
findings.fix_hint: Log a one-liner when JSON.parse fails (line 105) with the line index. Either return degraded:true on outer catch or log to console.error. Same pattern as audit-event.ts 'degraded' flag.

findings.title: loadStream for history failure in runButlerLoopBody swallowed with warn-only (no degradation flag)
findings.description: When event-bridge loadStream throws, history is empty but the loop proceeds. The owner-facing reply never indicates that the bot lost memory. The audit_event emission (e.g., a 'memory.degraded' action) would let owner queries see this. Other code paths use `degraded: true` flag (signal.ts:41, replay.ts:84).
findings.evidence: wechat-inbound-butler.ts:325-334: try { ... bridge.loadStream(...) } catch (err) { logger.warn(...) } — no flag, no audit emit.
findings.fix_hint: Add `historyDegraded: true` to initialTraces and emit an audit_event with action='memory.degraded' on catch.

findings.title: isPendingApprovalOutcome: 'pendingApproval' in outcome check without shape validation
findings.description: Type guard checks only `outcome.ok === false && 'pendingApproval' in outcome && outcome.pendingApproval !== undefined`. The TS extract `Extract<ToolExecutionOutcome, { pendingApproval: unknown }>` claims the shape, but at runtime an outcome with `pendingApproval: null` or `pendingApproval: 42` (defensive) would pass. Downstream code accesses `.pendingApproval.stepId` — a TypeError waiting to happen if the shape drifts.
findings.evidence: approval-resume.ts:34-42: returns true if 'pendingApproval' in outcome && !==undefined. consumers: subagent-worker.ts:351 `rawOutcome.pendingApproval.stepId`, wechat-inbound-butler.ts:639 `outcome.pendingApproval.stepId`.
findings.fix_hint: Add explicit `typeof outcome.pendingApproval === 'object' && outcome.pendingApproval !== null && typeof outcome.pendingApproval.stepId === 'string'` check. Then `.stepId` access is type-safe.

findings.title: tool-result cast on LLM tool call args: silent type widening at chokepoint
findings.description: subagent-worker.ts:349 calls `toolExecutor.execute(def, args as Record<string, unknown>)`. The upstream `args` is `Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>` (port signature) but the executor may take `Record<string, unknown>` (mutable). The cast strips readonly. Same pattern in wechat-inbound-butler.ts:565. Not a runtime bug but a TS escape hatch that the tool runtime should be designed to accept without the cast.
findings.evidence: subagent-worker.ts:349: const rawOutcome = await toolExecutor.execute(def, args as Record<string, unknown>). wechat-inbound-butler.ts:565: toolArgs as Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>. D60 T3.1 audit already widened the ConversationLoopToolCall type to drop the cast; same fix could be applied here.
findings.fix_hint: Widen the toolExecutor.execute signature in capability-boundary.ts:24 to accept `Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>`. Drop both casts.

findings.title: as unknown as DbTx double-cast in two appendAuditEventInTx/transitionRunStatusInTx sites
findings.description: After a runtime guard on `tx` (typeof insert/update === 'function'), the code casts via `tx as unknown as DbTx`. The runtime guard already proves the shape; the cast is the TS escape hatch. Acceptable but a `DbTx` narrowing via `as DbTx` (single cast) would suffice.
findings.evidence: runtime-store.ts:476-479 and 495-498 — same pattern at two sites.
findings.fix_hint: Change to `tx as DbTx` (single cast) — the runtime guard already satisfies TS structural rules. Or define a `function isDbTx(tx: unknown): tx is DbTx` and use it in both places.

findings.title: wechat-quality-gate's argv.timeoutMs / exit code is a number coerced from string without validation
findings.description: runArgv accepts timeoutMs but no upper bound check; if the caller passes a huge value (Number overflow) or a negative value, the spawn timer silently fires late or never. The 300_000 default is a magic number duplicated at apps/api/src/dev-quality-gate.ts:67, project-knowledge-sources-config.ts:65. Three sites, same magic number.
findings.evidence: wechat-quality-gate.ts:67 default fallback `300_000`; dev-quality-gate.ts:67 `300_000`; project-knowledge-sources-config.ts:65 `300_000`.
findings.fix_hint: Extract a `DEFAULT_QUALITY_GATE_TIMEOUT_MS = 300_000` constant in a shared module (e.g., packages/domain). Add `timeoutMs > 0` validation in runArgv.

findings.title: tools.ts has 4 separate Math.min(20, Math.max(1, Math.floor(limitRaw))) limit-normalizer copies
findings.description: Limit normalization duplicated at lines 134, 579, 613, 672. Each is `Math.min(N, Math.max(1, Math.floor(limitRaw)))` with a different N. A `clampLimit(raw, max, fallback)` helper would close 4 sites.
findings.evidence: tools.ts:134 `Math.min(Math.floor(limitRaw), 20)`; 579 `Math.min(20, Math.max(1, Math.floor(limitRaw)))`; 613 `Math.min(10, Math.max(1, Math.floor(limitRaw)))`; 672 `Math.min(20, Math.max(1, Math.floor(limitRaw)))`.
findings.fix_hint: Extract `function clampLimit(raw: string | undefined, max: number, fallback: number): number` and use at all 4 sites.

findings.title: Durable memory store skips redaction 'by design' — but no test asserts the gap
findings.description: Comment at line 17 says '消息内容不做落库脱敏（内存非耐久转录）'. By design. However, if a future engineer wires createInMemoryRuntimeStore into a non-test path, secrets would persist unredacted. A runtime guard or README warning would close this.
findings.evidence: memory/runtime-store.ts:17 explicit design note. Production runtime-store.ts:28 has redactStoredContent + line 460/486 calls redactTraceValue on audit detail.

findings.title: auditFatigueReader hardcodes actor='owner' (SEC-013) — no channel routing
findings.description: readRecent maps every event's actor to literal 'owner'. Cross-channel scenarios (wechat + telegram) cannot distinguish per-channel fatigue. D69 T3 closed SO-009 for wechat-inbound-butler but the reader itself is the bottleneck — multi-channel signals all flatten to 'owner'. Per the spec §3.1 cross-channel consolidation, this defeats the audit trail.
findings.evidence: audit-reader.ts:54-60: events.map((e) => ({ ... actor: 'owner' ... })). CQ-035 in docstring: 'audit-fatigue.ts TODO(D65+) for session lookup'. The D-cross-channel consistency scenario in acceptance (52/52) was deferred to D70+ per MEMORY.md.
findings.fix_hint: Map e.subject (or e.actor from the audit pipeline) to the reader's actor field. If the audit_event already carries subject=ownerSubject (per D58 T1), use that directly instead of overwriting.

findings.title: REPLAY_WINDOW_HOURS = 24: magic number without operator override
findings.description: Replay window is hardcoded to 24 hours. If an owner asks for replay of an event 25h old, the API returns 'event not found in 24h window' — and there's no env var to widen it. The listFatigueSequences takes windowSeconds from query, but replayFatigueSequence doesn't.
findings.evidence: replay.ts:24: const REPLAY_WINDOW_HOURS = 24. replay.ts:93: const events = await reader.readRecent(REPLAY_WINDOW_HOURS * 60 * 60 * 1000). No env override.
findings.fix_hint: Add `replayWindowHours` parameter to the route, defaulting to REPLAY_WINDOW_HOURS, and allow env var BUTLER_V5_REPLAY_WINDOW_HOURS.

findings.title: execute-tool-with-fatigue.ts:35 — unhandled PolicyDecision action throw has no shared type guard
findings.description: default: throw new Error(`unhandled PolicyDecision action: ${(decision as { action: string }).action}`) — same exact line in inline-approval-wiring.ts:44. Duplicated. A `assertNever(x: never): never` helper would centralize the exhaustiveness check.
findings.evidence: execute-tool-with-fatigue.ts:34-36; inline-approval-wiring.ts:43-45. Both inline `(decision as { action: string }).action` cast.
findings.fix_hint: Add `function assertNever(x: never): never { throw new Error('unhandled case: ' + JSON.stringify(x)) }` to a shared types file. Use in both places.
